A veil over the centre screen so maps and menus are less bright at night. Never drawn on the HUD or the instrument cluster.
How dark the veil is. 100 blocks touches.
0 is pure black. Higher is a lighter veil.
Higher shifts the veil toward amber.
On: the app underneath still receives taps. Off: the veil blocks them.
Tap to turn the veil on or off. Drag right or down for darker, left or up for lighter. Hold, then drag to move it. Orange when the veil is on.
Turns the veil on and off by itself. Untested on the car: 7xDash shipped its clock version as experimental. A tap on the moon holds until the next change.
Opacity 90%%, brightness 0, warmth 0, touches pass through. The veil stays on or off as it is.
Allow Veil to draw over other apps
The veil and the moon button are windows over other apps. The head unit has to allow that once.
This head unit has no settings page for it. From a computer with adb connected to the car, run:\n\n%1$s
Picture hidden while driving. Sound keeps playing.
Allow Veil to draw over other apps to show the iPhone screen.
Playing a video from the iPhone
Stays on after a restart if you leave it on.
The name the iPhone shows in its Screen Mirroring list.

1. Put the iPhone and the car on the same Wi-Fi. The usual way is to join the iPhone\'s Personal Hotspot from the car.\n2. On the iPhone, open Control Center and tap Screen Mirroring.\n3. Choose “%1$s”.
The iPhone screen opens in a floating window. Drag it to move, pinch to resize, push it to a side to dock it, tap the strip to bring it back, double-tap for small or large, and tap × to stop.

The picture hides whenever the car is in gear or moving; the sound keeps playing. Apps with copy protection (Netflix, Disney+, Apple TV) show a black picture. Video casting from an app\'s AirPlay button arrives in step 4.
Can\'t connect? Open http://%1$s/info in Safari on the iPhone (the page may stay blank). The Network page shows whether it reached the car.
The receiver is starting, or the car has no network address yet.
Why the iPhone might not see it
Nothing in the way: the receiver is on a Wi-Fi network and answers lookups itself. If the iPhone still does not list it, make sure it is on the same network, then turn Wi-Fi off and on on the iPhone.
The receiver is off. Turn it on from the AirPlay page.

The car is not on any Wi-Fi network, so there is no network the iPhone can share with it. On the iPhone turn on Personal Hotspot, then join it from the car\'s Wi-Fi settings. The car\'s own mobile data cannot be used: the iPhone cannot reach it.

Veil could not take over the lookup port (5353), so the head unit\'s own responder answers for it. On the 7X that responder gives out an internal address, and the iPhone may list the receiver but fail to connect. Try turning the receiver off and on again.
The car\'s Wi-Fi reports no multicast support, which the iPhone\'s lookup needs. The receiver may not be listed.
Veil may not draw over other apps yet, so the iPhone can connect but no picture will show. Allow it from the AirPlay or Dim page.
The car\'s Wi-Fi is a router, not the iPhone\'s hotspot. That works when the iPhone is on the same router. On the road, use the iPhone\'s Personal Hotspot.
Gear and speed: not readable right now. The picture is treated as parked and stays visible.
